children: U.S. Treasury and equity returns are moving in the same direction again in 2026, Bank of America Global Research said, a shift that is eroding one of the core reasons investors held bonds alongside stocks.
A BofA chart of average U.S. 10 Year Treasury yields
versus the 60-day correlation between those yields and the S&P 500 (

) shows the relationship flipping positive this year. That pattern last dominated in earlier high-rate decades. From 2000 through 2019 — the so-called secular stagnation stretch of fast globalization and unusually low inflation — bonds and stocks typically did not travel together. A 2%–3% yield was treated almost as a bonus for owning duration.

That era’s hedge is fading. When both asset classes rise and fall together, the portfolio-smoothing benefit of bonds shrinks. BofA argues allocators may therefore demand higher yields before rotating capital wholesale into fixed income. Official buying can cap a sharp backup in rates, the note added, but that does not automatically restore the old diversification case.
